Analyze an augmented p-rep design

Source: R/augmented_prep.R
analyze_augmented_prep_design.Rd

Fits the fixed-effects incomplete-block model: y = mean + location + block(location) + genotype + error. For resolvable designs (a replicate column with more than one replicate per location) the model is y = mean + location + replicate(location) + block(replicate, location) + genotype + error. With genotype_by_location = "fixed" (or TRUE) a fixed genotype-by-location interaction is added after genotypes; the error is then estimated only from the p-rep entries, as in a per-location analysis with pooled error (Williams, Piepho and Whitaker, 2011, Section 3). With genotype_by_location = "random" the interaction is a random effect, as recommended by the paper when locations are a sample of environments, and the model is fitted by REML with 'lme4'. Sums of squares are sequential, in the order above. Degrees of freedom in the formatted ANOVA are those estimable from the observed (non-missing) plots, so F-tests stay valid when plots are missing. For a complete, connected design they equal the design formulas reported in anova_df, which use total plots (n), locations (l), incomplete blocks (b), and genotypes (v). Terms with a single level in the data (for example the location term in a single-location trial) are left out of the model and shown with 0 df.

Usage

analyze_augmented_prep_design(
  data,
  response,
  genotype_col = "all_entries",
  location_col = "location",
  block_col = "block",
  entry_type_col = "entry_type",
  extra_repeat_col = "is_extra_repeat",
  repeated_at_col = "repeated_at",
  control_col = "is_control",
  replicate_col = "replicate",
  genotype_by_location = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A complete augmented p-rep design data frame, usually design$design from augmented_prep_design(), or an object returned by augmented_prep_design(), with a response column added.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

genotype_col

Name of the genotype/treatment column.

location_col

Name of the location column.

block_col

Name of the incomplete block column. Block numbers may repeat across locations; blocks are treated as nested within locations.

entry_type_col

Optional entry type column. Used only for genotype summaries.

extra_repeat_col

Optional extra-repeat indicator column. Used only for genotype summaries.

repeated_at_col

Optional column identifying where each entry is repeated. Used only for genotype summaries.

control_col

Optional control flag column. Used only for genotype summaries.

replicate_col

Optional replicate (superblock) column. When present and a location has more than one replicate, replicates nested within locations are fitted, and blocks are nested within replicates. Set to NULL to ignore it.

genotype_by_location

Genotype-by-location interaction in a multi-location analysis: "none" (default, or FALSE), "fixed" (or TRUE), or "random" (needs the 'lme4' package). With "fixed", adjusted means are averaged over locations. With "random", adjusted means are the genotype BLUEs from the mixed model, variance_components gives the REML estimates, and the ANOVA table is the fixed-interaction table, whose genotype-by-location and error mean squares show the size of the interaction.

Value

An object of class augmented_prep_analysis: a list with

input, formula, model

The column mapping, model formula, and the lm fit.

anova, anova_df, anova_formatted

Sequential ANOVA (estimable df), design df formulas, and a formatted ANOVA table.

plot_results

The input data with fitted values and residuals.

genotype_summary

One row per genotype with raw, fitted, and adjusted means and the standard error of the adjusted mean.

adjusted_means

Genotypes ranked by adjusted mean (best first).

adjusted_means_vcov

Covariance matrix of the estimable adjusted means, used by analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage() for weighting.

diagnostics

Error df, residual standard deviation, R-squared, mean_sed (mean standard error of a difference between two adjusted means), lsd_5pct (the matching least significant difference), and flags for rank deficiency or a saturated fit.

variance_components, mixed_model

For genotype_by_location = "random": REML variance components and the lmerMod fit; otherwise NULL.

message

A note when F-tests or adjusted means are not estimable.

Adjusted means

Genotype effects are fixed, so the adjusted means are best linear unbiased estimates (BLUEs): the genotype effect plus the average location and block effect over all observed plots, i.e. the expected value of the genotype in an average plot of the trial. They remove the advantage or penalty of the blocks and locations where each entry happened to be planted, so use adjusted_mean (not raw_mean) to rank and select entries. Differences between adjusted means are the same as those from emmeans on the fitted model. With genotype_by_location = "fixed" the genotype-by-location effects are averaged over locations, weighting each location by its share of the observed plots. With "random", standard errors come from the REML covariance of the fixed effects, which includes the genotype-by-location variance; lsd_5pct uses the error df of the fixed-interaction model as an approximation.

Per-location analysis

Williams, Piepho and Whitaker (2011) suggest analysing each location with an incomplete-block model. Pass the rows of one location, e.g. analyze_augmented_prep_design(data[data$location == "A", ], "yield"). augmented_prep_design() keeps the blocks of every location connected, so this is estimable whenever the location has enough p-rep plots.

Examples

design <- augmented_prep_design(
  treatments = paste0("G", seq_len(8)),
  locations = c("Loc1", "Loc2"),
  block_size = 4,
  n_duplicate_per_location = c(Loc1 = 2, Loc2 = 2),
  n_candidates = 3,
  seed = 123
)

design_data <- design$design
design_data$yield <- rnorm(nrow(design_data), mean = 100, sd = 10)
analysis <- analyze_augmented_prep_design(design_data, response = "yield")
analysis
